newsitem.title: BELGIUM: STILL TICKS TO GO BEFORE BELGIAN OLOS LURE BUYERS.
newsitem.headline: STILL TICKS TO GO BEFORE BELGIAN OLOS LURE BUYERS.

text.p: The yield on the benchmark 10-year Belgian government bond still has scope to rise before major buyers will emerge, dealers said on Thursday.

The bond market was soft again on Thursday after Wednesday's mild recovery with most players, cautious before Friday's release of key U.S. jobless data for March [US-ECI], reluctant to commit their money either way.

"There are small buyers in every price correction, but for institutionals to come out yields might have to reach 6.25 percent," a dealer said. The benchmark 10-year OLO yielded 6.17 percent late on Thursday, up from 6.14 late on Wednesday.
He said that target might be hit in one or two weeks.

Bond prices eased on Thursday morning after a firmer start in line with other European markets as stronger than expected German industrial output data [DE-ECI] caught players off balance. But volumes were thin with traders and end-investors wary of parting with their holdings at present levels.
Other dealers said it was unclear how far prices needed to fall before buyers would emerge. "We will test lower levels -- there is not much support there," said one.
The yield spread over 10-year German Bunds firmed by one basis point to 14, falling faster than Bunds.
Dealers said Friday's release of the U.S. monthly jobs data would be used by most as an excuse to square their books.
U.S. payrolls data are forecast to show that 182,000 new non-farm jobs were created in March, after 339,000 in February.
While such a number would be bond-positive, average hourly earnings, expected to have grown by 0.4 percent in March after 0.2 percent in February, could upset the apple cart.

News U.S. weekly jobless claims rose slightly last week, exceeding forecasts, while the four-week moving average, which is viewed as a more accurate indicator than the more volatile weekly figures, also rose slightly, did little to calm nerves.

While another 25 basis point rate hike in the U.S., possibly as soon as May, had already been discounted, it remained tough trying to convince players there was value at the shorter end and that buyers should act now before other investors switched from weak stock markets, dealers said.

Analysts have said that with expectations of U.S. monetary policy remaining the driving force in the run-up to the next U.S. Federal Reserve policy meetings on May 20 and July 1 and 2 OLO trade would likely remain choppy.
But a re-focusing on European fundamentals could push the benchmark yield down again to 5.75 to 6.10 percent by end-June.
They said people were getting too negative about the outlook for monetary policy in the U.S., while forgetting about low inflation in Germany and Belgium and modest economic growth.
Analysts expected Belgian unemployment to rise in the second quarter, meaning consumer confidence was not likely to pick up.
They forecast the Bundesbank would leave all its key interest rates unchanged in the second quarter, with the repo rate steady at 3.00 percent.
In this scenario the National Bank of Belgium would not have to adjust its key central rate, also at 3.00 percent.
